detail:
A 2026 JAMA review by Camilleri summarizes gastroparesis as a disorder in which the stomach empties too slowly despite no mechanical obstruction. The most common symptoms are nausea, early fullness after eating only a small amount, bloating, and vomiting, sometimes of food eaten hours earlier. Many cases are idiopathic, meaning no cause is identified; diabetes is the most common known cause.

The review describes gastric emptying scintigraphy as the criterion standard test: retention of more than 10% of a standardized meal at 4 hours supports the diagnosis. Current guidance from the American College of Gastroenterology (2022) and the American Gastroenterological Association (2025) frames both testing and the treatment ladder that follows it.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about evaluation for persistent nausea or early fullness.
summary: A JAMA review describes gastroparesis as delayed emptying of the stomach without any blockage, most often idiopathic or related to diabetes; the reference diagnostic test is a gastric emptying study showing more than 10% of a meal still in the stomach after 4 hours.
takeaways: nausea and feeling full after small meals are hallmark symptoms
a 4-hour gastric emptying study is the reference test
diabetes is the most common known cause
diagnosis needs a clinician; symptoms overlap many gi conditions
title: Gastroparesis: when the stomach empties too slowly
